Call par kaise bolein, kaise jawab dein: How to talk on a call, how to respond and what to say — from the phone screen to the video round
Call se pehle ki taiyari aur shuruaat: Preparing for the call and the opening
Zyadatar interviews ab phone ya video pa: Most interviews now happen by phone or video. In the first round (the recruiter's **phone screen**) you get 15–30 minutes — so the **first 30 seconds** leave a big impression.
Background awaaz se samajhna mushkil hot: Background noise makes you hard to understand
Awaaz saaf jaati hai, echo nahi: Your voice is clear, with no echo
Beech mein call na kate: So the call does not drop midway
Sawaal ka jawab dete waqt yaad rahega: Helps you remember things while answering
Padhna nahi — bas yaad dilane ke liye: Not to read from — just to jog your memory
Phone par **pehle aap bolte ho**, to con: On a phone call **you speak first**, so speak confidently and clearly. Keep a short script:
Agar recruiter poochhe 'Is this a good t: If the recruiter asks 'Is this a good time?' and you are busy, say it plainly: 'Could we schedule it for later today? I would like to give you my full attention.' This sounds professional.
Camera aankh ki level par rakho, roshni: Keep the camera at eye level, with the light **in front of** you (not behind), and look **at the camera** while answering, not at the screen. Smile and say 'Hello' at the start.
Phone call par pehle kaun bolta hai?: On a phone call, who speaks first?
Call utha kar pehle aap bolte ho: 'Hello: You answer first: 'Hello, this is ... speaking.'
Notes yaad dilane ke liye hote hain, pad: Notes are to remind you, not to read from.
Agar abhi baat karna mushkil ho?: What if you cannot talk right now?
Video call mein kahan dekhna chahiye?: Where should you look on a video call?
Camera ki taraf dekhne se aankh ka sampa: Looking at the camera creates eye contact.
Call par kaise bolein: speed, pause aur: How to talk on a call: pace, pauses and clear speech
Call par face aur hand ke ishare nahi di: On a call nobody can see your face or hands — everything goes through your **voice**. So speak a little **slower, clearer and in shorter sentences**.
Normal se thoda dheere; call par awaaz c: A bit slower than normal; audio gets compressed on calls.
Beech mein mat bolo; 1 second ruk kar ja: Do not interrupt; wait 1 second, then start your answer.
Ek sentence = ek idea. Lambe sentences m: One sentence = one idea. Long sentences make you lose your way.
Sochne ke liye 2–3 second ka pause lo; ': Take a 2–3 second pause to think; it is better than 'umm'.
Lambe jawab ke baad: 'Does that answer y: After a long answer: 'Does that answer your question?'
Call par sunai na dena ya samajh na aana: Not hearing or not understanding on a call is **normal**. It is better to **ask** than to guess and answer wrongly. Interviewers see that as a good sign.
'What?' ya 'Huh?' mat bolo — rude lagta: Do not say 'What?' or 'Huh?' — it sounds rude. Always say 'Sorry, could you repeat that?'
Jawab ka resham: Haan, Wajah, Example: The answer thread: Yes, Reason, Example
Har jawab ke liye 3 hisse: **Seedha jawa: Give every answer 3 parts: a **direct answer** (1 sentence) → a **reason** (1 sentence) → an **example** (1–2 sentences). That makes an answer of 20–30 seconds.
Call par kaise bolna chahiye?: How should you speak on a call?
Call par awaaz compress hoti hai, isliye: Audio is compressed on calls, so slow and clear.
Sawaal samajh na aaye to?: If you did not understand the question?
Sochne ke liye kya karein?: What do you do to think?
This phrase buys you thinking time.
Confirm karna interviewer ko control det: Checking in gives the interviewer control.
Kaise jawab dein: aam sawaal aur kya bol: How to respond: common call questions and what to say
Phone screening mein sawaal lagbhag hame: Phone screens ask almost the same questions every time. Keep a **ready structure** for each — change the words, keep the structure.
2. 'Why are you looking for a change?': 2. 'Why are you looking for a change?'
Purane company ki **burai mat karo**. Se: Never **criticise** your old company. Talk about learning and growth.
Pehle **range** batao ya poochho ki comp: Give a **range**, or ask what the company's range is. Add **'depending on the role and responsibilities'** to the number.
5. 'Do you have any questions for us?': 5. 'Do you have any questions for us?'
Kabhi bhi 'No' mat bolo. Kam se kam **ek: Never just say 'No'. Ask at least **one** question.
Jawab mein **'I'** bolo, 'we' nahi — int: Say **'I'** in your answers, not 'we' — the interviewer wants to know your role.
Do not criticise; talk about learning.
Notice period kaise batate hain?: How do you state your notice period?
'Tell me about yourself' kitne second?: How long for 'Tell me about yourself'?
Jab kuch gadbad ho: awaaz, lag, ghabraha: When something goes wrong: audio, lag and nerves
Call mein dikkat aana normal hai. Interv: Problems on calls are normal. Interviewers watch **how you handle** them — it can leave a good impression.
Jawab na aaye to: When you do not know the answer
Kabhi jhooth ya andaaza mat do. Sach bol: Never lie or guess wildly. Be honest and show **willingness to learn**.
Jawab se pehle **ek lambi saans** lo. Dh: Take **one deep breath** before answering. Speak slowly. If you slip, just say 'Let me rephrase that.' and carry on. Nobody speaks perfectly.
Jawab nahi pata to?: If you do not know the answer?
A short correction, then move on.
Call khatam karna aur follow-up: Closing the call and following up
Call ka **ant** bhi utna hi zaroori hai: The **end** of the call matters as much as the start. In the last 30 seconds you show interest and ask about the next step.
Thank-you email (call ke baad, 24 ghante: Thank-you email (within 24 hours after the call)
Email chhota rakho — 4 se 5 line. Ek spe: Keep the email short — 4 to 5 lines. Mention one specific thing from the call so they remember you.
Agar jawab na aaye: If you do not hear back
Pehla follow-up **5–7 din baad** karo, e: Send the first follow-up **5–7 days later**, once or twice at most.
Thank-you email kab bhejein?: When do you send the thank-you email?
Agle step ke baare mein poochna professi: Asking about next steps is professional.
Email kitna lamba?: How long should the email be?
